author: Jake Stiles STAFF WRITER
title: The Bridge Sports Complex marks fifth anniversary with celebration Thursday | Bridgeport News | wvnews.com
text:
BRIDGEPORT, W.Va. — The Bridge Sports Complex will mark its fifth anniversary Thursday with a community celebration highlighting the facility’s growth, expanded programming and future plans.
The anniversary event will be held from 3 to 6 p.m. on the indoor turf at the CityNet Center and is open to members, day-pass holders and guests.
Vendors will offer free services, including blood pressure and cholesterol screenings from WVU Medicine United Hospital Center, chair massages from Revitalize Health & Med Spa, gait analysis from Bridgeport Running and bike testing from Pike Street Bikes. Stretch Zone will provide complimentary stretching sessions. And group fitness instructors from The Bridge will be available throughout the event.
The celebration coincides with a weeklong promotion running through June 28. Members can receive free T-shirts, discounted Clip n’ Climb sessions and enter a drawing for a one-year individual gold membership.
Droo Callahan, general manager of The Bridge, said Thursday’s celebration will include the burial of a time capsule, though organizers are keeping the event relatively low-key.
“We’re just doing a mild celebration to recognize that we’ve existed for five years,” Callahan said.
Since opening in 2021, The Bridge has adjusted operations to better balance community use with tournaments and special events.
Callahan, who joined the facility in September 2020, said one of the biggest improvements has been the use of live online schedules to help patrons avoid conflicts.
“For the first couple of years we had hit some bumps in the road because, you know, somebody came in to play basketball or to swim, but we had a swim meet or we had a basketball tournament. But we’ve been able to be a little bit more efficient with getting schedules online that are live,” Callahan said.
“It’s kind of worked out, I think, for the best of both worlds — both our community and then patrons that want to come in from outside the community,” he said.
Joe Shuttleworth, Bridgeport’s interim city manager and parks and recreation director, said the complex’s fitness operation has exceeded initial projections, particularly through participation in SilverSneakers, a program that provides qualifying seniors access to the facility through their insurance plans.
“The one that’s kind of just blown out of the pro forma is the amount of people and revenue we receive from the fitness side of things,” Shuttleworth said. “It’s become very popular with our senior community.”
Shuttleworth also credited staff for developing unique programming that attracts visitors from outside the region, including card trading shows, a reptile expo and a boxing event planned for July.
“They’ve been very, very thinking outside the box,” Shuttleworth said. “I think we offer a different experience than just your normal gym.”
Former Bridgeport Mayor Andy Lang said the complex has greatly exceeded expectations since planning began nearly a decade ago.
“I think it has exceeded expectations by at least 200%,” he said. “It’s almost double what we anticipated it was going to be back in 2017.”
Lang said part of the facility’s success stems from the lack of similar regional venues when it opened.
Looking ahead, Callahan said the focus will be on maximizing recent additions, including a new multi-use turf field expected to be fully operational by late this year or early next year. Additional expansion opportunities remain under consideration.
“We still have a couple of different plots we’re looking to attack,” he said.
